mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 3.5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 1% signals an emergency monetary easing, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 1% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS drops below 1% in a month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of more than 1% in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) in the same month signals a synchronized expansion in demand components, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such synchronized demand expansions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such sustained payroll growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.4% for five consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side recovery, which improves corporate capacity and profit margins, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.4% for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such sustained INDPRO expansions (t-test p > 0.05).
